extracted.intended_audience: arXiv platform engineers, system architects, developers, moderators, and administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Architecture and requirements for the arXiv submission & moderation subsystem: design goals, component responsibilities, interfaces, and operational constraints for implementing accession, QA/moderation, automation, and event-based auditing of submissions up to announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accession via multiple interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem must accept submission of e-print content and metadata via multiple interfaces, including interfaces provided by trusted third-party platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports both interactive (UI) and programmatic (REST API, bulk deposit) submission paths; must allow trusted external clients to deposit on behalf of users with explicit authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance tools and moderation workflows
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tools and workflows to screen submissions (moderation) prior to announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes manual moderator interfaces for flags, comments, proposals and automated QA checks; supports iterative submitter revisions and moderator-driven reclassification/comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensible automation for moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: An extensible system for automating parts of the moderation process must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architecture must support configurable rule-based automation (agent-run processes) that can be extended to add or modify automated checks and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-based audit log
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an event-based log of all submission and moderation activity related to a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events should be emitted for submission lifecycle actions to support auditing, reproducible state reconstruction, and downstream processes; events are used as the primary source of truth where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of responsibility up to announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem is responsible for all submission-related activities up to (but not including) announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and interfaces should stop at handoff to the announcement agent/process; downstream announcement steps are separate services consuming submission outputs/events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-agent synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem must sensibly incorporate input from, and synchronize the activities of, a variety of human and non-human agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must coordinate actions between submitters, moderators, administrators, automated processes, and third-party clients; avoid inconsistent state and ensure clear ownership of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator auditability of submission state changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators must be able to audit all changes to submission state in the subsystem (e.g., actions by submitters, moderators, automated processes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative UIs showing event history, annotations, and the ability to inspect who/what caused state transitions; persistent event records are required for auditing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configurable automated rules and processes for admins
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators must be able to configure automated rules and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose administrative controls for enabling/disabling and tuning automation rules executed by the submission agent; changes should be auditable and have safe defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support many interfaces and third-party integrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem must support future development of potentially many alternative interfaces for submission and moderation, including interfaces developed and operated by trusted third-parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design APIs and authentication/authorization so third parties can integrate safely; ensure backward compatibility and stable API gateway controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-volume throughput and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem must be able to support a high volume of activity (example: ~11,000 submissions/month with expected growth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architect for scaling (cloud-ready storage, queues, stateless services) and plan capacity growth (expected ≥10%/year). Performance and reliability under load are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support future operational and policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsystem must make it easier to support future operational and policy changes around submission content, quality assurance, metadata, and other areas of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for flexibility: modular services, clear data models, event-driven hooks to change processes without large rewrites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompose functionality into utility services
rubrics_metrics.description: Major functional components should be decomposed into independent utility services that are agnostic about the submissions themselves (classification, overlap detection, compilation, file management, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility services provide reusable functionality via APIs and should not embed submission business logic; keeps the system modular and replaceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core submission package as authoritative write API
rubrics_metrics.description: A core submission package provides the foundational logic and is the only mechanism for writing submission data to the Submission database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All UI and agent services must use the core package to perform canonical submission operations (events/commands); prevents divergent write paths and enforces business rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core interface services built on core package
rubrics_metrics.description: Core submission interface services (UIs and APIs) must be built on top of the core submission package to support submission and moderation workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interface services should delegate state mutations to the core package to guarantee consistent application of business logic and event emission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent framework for rules and conditional processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an agent which defines rules and conditional processes based on submission events to orchestrate automated backend processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent must observe event streams, match rules, execute processes asynchronously, and emit resulting events; configurable rules for triggering processes are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticated user capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticated users must be able to submit e-prints, view and amend submission status, preview submissions, and edit source files via the UI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UI must provide metadata entry, source package upload/edits, previewing, and integration with compilation services to help prepare announcement-ready submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderators (authenticated users with moderator role) must be able to screen and curate submissions via a moderation interface and generate comments, flags, proposals, and annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation UI should provide workflows for proposing reclassification, commenting, flagging, and requesting submitter/admin input; moderator actions must be recorded as events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator management capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators must be able to audit and manage the submission platform, including behavior of automated processes and policies, via an administrative interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admin interfaces should allow configuring policies/automation, intervening on submission content/metadata, and acting on moderator proposals with visibility into event history.

rubrics_metrics.name: API gateway enforcement and REST API
rubrics_metrics.description: All API access must pass through the arXiv API gateway; the submission system provides a RESTful API for programmatic use with client authentication and explicit user authorization for deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: API exposes backend services (file management, compilation, classification) and must enforce authorization at gateway level; supports bulk and single submission deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-hook notification support for clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a web-hook notification service that pushes updates in submission state to authorized API clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow clients to register callbacks; event consumer implementation should guarantee delivery semantics and security (authentication/authorization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator-controlled exposure of backend services
rubrics_metrics.description: Backend services exposed via the API gateway must have access explicitly authorized by administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service-level authorization and admin-managed permissions are required to limit which clients/services can call sensitive backend endpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission database responsibilities and event primary source
rubrics_metrics.description: The Submission database must persist operational and core descriptive metadata; the primary source of truth for the state of each submission is a set of transformation events; derivative representations are stored for querying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store both events and derived projections; support migrations from legacy DBs and a clear plan for event-sourcing as the canonical model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical commands/events to canonicalize operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a set of commands (events) that canonicalize operations on submissions and serve as the basis for composing rule-based QA processing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands/events should be well-defined, versioned, and used consistently by UI, API, and agent components to ensure consistent behavior across the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with utility services and notification broker
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission core must provide service integration modules for working with utility services (compilation, classifier, etc.) and integrate with a notification broker for event dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a broker (e.g., Kinesis) for event propagation; utility integrations should be encapsulated in modules to isolate dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent responsibilities: orchestration, tracking, conditional execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent must orchestrate automated backend processes based on submission events, keep track of what processes have been carried out and their outcomes, and provide a framework for defining conditions under which processes run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes should run asynchronously, emit events back to the stream, and the agent should rely on a task queue (e.g., Celery/Redis) for execution management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core interface services must update submission state via core package
rubrics_metrics.description: Core interface services (Submission UI, Submission API service, Moderation UI, Administrative UI) must integrate with the Submission database to modify state via the Submission core package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interfaces must not perform direct DB mutations; they should invoke core package commands to ensure consistent event emission and state transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: File management: verification and sanitization
rubrics_metrics.description: File management service is responsible for ensuring the safety and suitability of uploaded files by performing verification and sanitization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept uploads, sanitize/verify contents, and present sanitized artifacts to other services; support different storage backends (SFS on-prem, EFS/AWS in cloud).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation/build service with logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a compilation service that builds sanitized upload packages into PDF, PostScript, and other formats and makes compilation logs available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compilation should use an arXiv TeX tree, back storage (e.g., S3), and expose logs for submitter feedback on failures/warnings to help produce announcement-ready submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain text extraction for downstream QA
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract plain text from PDFs (and produce normalized PSV tokenized text) to support overlap detection and classification services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make both raw extracted text and normalized tokenized forms available to other services for machine processing (similarity, classification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap detection for duplicate detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate on extracted text and metadata to detect possibly duplicate submissions (overlap detection service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return candidates (announced e-prints) with a high degree of overlap for moderator inspection; integrate with event-driven QA checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification/autoclassifier service
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate on extracted plain text and metadata to propose categories for submitted papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifier outputs should be used as moderator aids and be auditable; integration example: FinalizeSubmission event triggers RunAutoclassifier process via the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification service for emails and UI configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification service must dispatch email notifications to submitters and moderators in response to submission events and provide UIs for end-user and administrator configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure delivery, configurable templates, and user-level preferences; tie notifications to event stream to ensure consistent triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-hook notification service implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mechanisms for API clients to register callbacks for submission events; consumer implemented using Kinesis Consumer Library and MultiLangDaemon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement secure callback registration, retry/delivery semantics, and authorization checks for registered clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-driven example: autoclassifier integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Example flow: FinalizeSubmission event emitted by Submission UI → Submission agent observes event and matches rule → agent runs RunAutoclassifier process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates rule-based, event-triggered automation; finalization should include attestation fields and produce events consumed by agent processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-sourcing goal: events as source of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an event-sourcing framework where the current state of a submission is generated from all events that have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan migration away from legacy components that write directly to DB; when achieved, applications should write events to the event controller and read state from the DB projections only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle legacy direct writes and interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Until legacy components are retired, changes made by direct DB mutations must be inferred/interpolated into the event stream (arxiv.submission.services.classic.interpolate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide interpolation mechanisms for reconciling legacy writes with event-sourced state; document limitations and data-migration strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid race conditions on event stream; enforce consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken not to persist events that are inconsistent with the current submission state; adopt optimistic locking/versioning and an event controller to reject mismatched-version events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim approach: rely on legacy DB atomic transactions and short-lived shared locks on related rows while committing events; long-term: event controller with version checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce event-generating applications' responsibility for state projection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimately, event-generating applications should only read state and write events to the event stream; responsibility for updating projected submission state should be moved to an event controller service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently, event-generating apps must both write events and update state due to legacy constraints; plan to centralize persistence/consistency logic in the event controller to preserve ACID guarantees and simplify producers.
